headline: ICE looks to sell Romulus warehouse initially planned for detention center
summary: In 2026, the U.S. government attempted to convert a Romulus warehouse into an ICE detention center, sparking local opposition and a lawsuit from Michigan's Attorney General. The plan was scrapped in June, and now the warehouse, along with six others, is being marketed for sale by a commercial real estate firm.

headline: Supporters of Barrett, Lawrence clash at dueling protests ahead of debate
summary: Supporters of Will Lawrence and Tom Barrett engaged in dueling protests in Lansing, Michigan, on October 5, 2026, with each side criticizing the other's political stance and record. Lawrence's supporters, "Spartans for Will," accused Barrett of being a status quo politician, while Barrett's supporters criticized Lawrence's associations with democratic socialists and his arrest record. The protests took place just 31 days before the 2026 general election, in which Lawrence and Barrett are running for the 7th Congressional District seat.

headline: ICE looks to sell two Pennsylvania warehouses and others initially planned for detention center
summary: The U.S. government plans to sell two former ICE detention center warehouses in Pennsylvania, with the Tremont facility initially purchased for $119.5M, now part of a seven-warehouse portfolio marketed by Cushman & Wakefield.

headline: Three criminal cases involving ICE hit the Supreme Judicial Court
summary: The Massachusetts Supreme Judicial Court heard arguments in three cases involving immigration enforcement during criminal proceedings. Prosecutors argued they have no duty to inform judges of potential ICE arrests, while defense attorneys argued judges should have power to order ICE to bring defendants to trial. The cases highlight challenges in balancing state criminal justice with federal immigration enforcement.

headline: Las redadas migratorias de Trump dejan al suroeste de Kansas buscando cómo seguir adelante
summary: Protests erupted in Dodge City, Kansas, following ICE raids targeting immigrant communities. Hundreds gathered, waving Mexican and American flags, demanding ICE's departure. Demonstrations also occurred outside Rep. Tracey Mann's office, with protesters chanting "Tracey Mann, ¿dónde estás? ¿Te necesitamos?" The unrest highlights the impact of immigration policies on local communities and economies.

headline: Danbury mayor calls white power rally participants ‘cowards’
summary: A dozen masked individuals held a "Keep New England White" sign near Danbury's police headquarters, shouting "White power" before dispersing. Mayor Roberto Alvez condemned the display, stating it was intended to incite fear in the diverse community but would not deter unity. The incident followed recent ICE raids in the city, with immigrant advocates linking the white supremacist rally to anti-immigrant sentiment. Police are investigating.

headline: Lamont touts CT response to Medicaid cuts, stops short of pledging funds
summary: Connecticut faces federal changes to Medicaid program HUSKY D, affecting around 108,000 residents. State steps in to protect coverage, funding $115M from emergency response fund, but Governor Lamont refrains from committing state dollars until federal responsibility is clearer. State working on systems to verify eligibility and ensure exemptions for "medically frail" individuals. Stamford city partners with local organizations to help residents stay covered, serving as a model for other municipalities. No direct mention of State Budget, but potential impacts on state's financial obligations for Medicaid and associated programs.

headline: Democrats more trusted on healthcare costs, survey shows
summary: A poll by KFF shows Democrats are more motivated to vote in midterms, with 63% feeling more motivated compared to 38% of Republicans. Democrats lead on addressing healthcare and abortion costs, while Republicans have an edge on immigration. Voters overwhelmingly favor a national health plan, though support drops when potential tax increases are mentioned. Most voters want healthcare system changes.

headline: How the Scarborough ICE facility is feeding the nationwide detention apparatus
summary: ICE detentions in Maine have surged under Trump's second term, with Scarborough facility overnight holds increasing from zero in 2023-2024 to eight in 2025 and 23 in 2026. Detainees are now frequently transferred out of state, with Massachusetts, New Hampshire, and southern facilities being common destinations.

headline: Poll: Moore sits with a comfortable 2-1 margin over Republican challenger Cox
summary: A new University of Maryland, Baltimore County poll finds Maryland Gov. Wes Moore (D) leading Republican nominee Dan Cox by 27 points, with Moore securing 51% and Cox at 24%. This wide margin is reminiscent of their 2022 race and could impact the upcoming debate on Oct. 6.

headline: Child dies from bacterial infection, state health department reports
summary: In Montana, a child died from an invasive Haemophilus influenzae type b infection, underscoring the importance of Hib vaccinations. The Montana Department of Public Health and Human Services urges parents to ensure their children are up-to-date with all recommended vaccines, including Hib. This tragic event highlights the ongoing need for public health efforts to promote vaccination and prevent such diseases.

headline: Montana health officials warn of severe risks as Fergus County confirms measles case
summary: Measles cases confirmed in Montana this year, including Fergus County's first case, highlighting concerns about declining vaccination rates. Montana's estimated measles vaccination rate among 2-year-olds is 86.3%, with national kindergarten rates dropping to 92.4%. In 2021, Montana passed HB 334, limiting health department access to student immunization records.

headline: South Dakota National Guard helps with more than 1,000 deportations since July 2025, governor says
summary: South Dakota's Governor Larry Rhoden has extended cooperation with ICE for paperwork processing by the National Guard until 2027, with 1,013 deportations processed since July 2025. The state has also trained troopers to question and detain undocumented immigrants, leading to 261 arrests.

headline: Arkansas lawmakers adopt recommendations for per-student school funding
summary: Arkansas's Joint Education Committee proposed a $238 million increase in public school funding over two years, raising per-student funding to $8,431 by 2028. This includes $26 million for dyslexia intervention and $14 million for high-cost occurrence students. Lawmakers will vote on these recommendations during the upcoming legislative session.
